pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/studio/_host/rooms.tsx:95 The live room marks the dock 'thinking' whenever the person's message is the newest event, and live.ts:12 plus the dock's canSendIn then refuse a send in that state, so a follow-up is refused while the agent works even though a durable ledger exists (say.ts appendOnce) and audio_inbox's `unanswered` would deliver several says at the agent's next safe point.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/studio/_host/rooms.tsx:95 Mid-unit input is refused at the surface (thinking -> dockStateOf 'thinking' -> canSendIn false). The technique allows that only where no durable record exists, and here one does: the say is appended keyed by turn id (say.ts:31).

app/(studio)/audio/studio/_host/StudioHost.tsx:82 When the scripted fixture answers in place of the agent, the operator surface names that producer ('scripted') rather than passing it off as a live agent.
app/(studio)/audio/studio/_live/presence.ts:36 Presence reads an env-named token (presence.ts:22) but only colours the pill; it gates no capability, and send stays possible either way.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:112 tools/list publishes every write tool to every token, but callTool refuses writes for a read-scope token (rpc.ts:78-79). The roster and the run-time refusal therefore do not come from one policy on one session, so the model is shown tools the executor will refuse.

techniques.evidence: app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:112 The refusal does resolve from the session's token scope (good source), but no roster filter derives from the same scope: a read token is handed write tools, 'a fluent invitation to fail'.

app/_server/mcp/tools/launch.ts:44 The live/spend guard judges a receipt the server recomputed, not a token or figure the agent carries. A non-free live ask becomes an operator-confirmed spend request the agent cannot raise.
app/_server/mcp/registry.ts:15 Tools are statically imported rows. No configuration or caller can name code to load.
